meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wish', paired with 'пожелать'.

related.gloss: not to would you like (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: May we come in? Good day, sir.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pizza' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free.

examples.text: Анатолий Иванович, тут доставка пиццы. Пишут, доставим за десять минут.
examples.trans: Anatoly Ivanovich, there's pizza delivery here. They write: we'll deliver in ten minutes.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning '(emphasis) after all, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'offer, proposal; sentence' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It's a good offer, of course.

examples.text: Значит, предложение такое. Ты мне говоришь, где твои сорок миллионов.
examples.trans: So, here's the offer. You tell me where your forty million is.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mum, mother' in everyday Russian.

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.en: to call, to phone; to ring
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'реагировать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to react, respond', paired with 'реагировать'.

examples.text: И как он на это отреагировал?
examples.trans: And how did he react to that?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Do you think that's really possible?
It's realistic to do that in a day.

examples.text: Я не шучу и реально сваливаю отсюда.
examples.trans: I am not joking and am seriously getting out of here.

говорить.gloss: to speak, to say, to talk

meanings.en: to speak, to say, to talk
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to speak, to say, to talk', paired with 'сказать'.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'бить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to beat up, thrash'.

related.gloss: not to to beat up (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Он избил писателя в зале ресторана.
examples.trans: He beat up the writer in the dining room of the restaurant.

examples.text: А потом он избил писателя Пелевина!
examples.trans: And then he beat up the writer Pelevin!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'in short; shorter', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Короче, Самсон, сегодня ты приводишь её к Димону.
examples.trans: In short, Samson, tonight you bring her to Dimon's place.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Подождите! Два дня — это же очень мало.
examples.trans: Hold on! Two days is far too little.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что? Ты мне ухо отрежешь?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what? Will you cut my ear off?

examples.text: А если я не скажу, то что?
examples.trans: And if I don't tell you, then what?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'сший'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('highest, supreme').

examples.trans: Everything is arranged at the highest level.

examples.text: Я всё устрою на высшем уровне.
examples.trans: I will arrange everything at the highest level.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'advantage, lead' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У вас по-прежнему есть хорошее преимущество.
examples.trans: You still have a good lead.

examples.text: О каком преимуществе ты сейчас говоришь?
examples.trans: What lead are you talking about now?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'war' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Read The Art of War, by Sun Tzu!
This book tells about the war.

examples.text: В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Last time I thought a war had started.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'пасть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to attack, to mug', paired with 'нападать'.

examples.text: Какие-то хулиганы вдруг напали на него.
И какие-то хулиганы вдруг напали на него. Не сильно, но человеку плохо.
examples.trans: And some hooligans suddenly attacked him. Not badly, of course, but the man feels unwell.

examples.text: И какие-то хулиганы вдруг напали на него.
examples.trans: And some hooligans suddenly attacked him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'enemy' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: С ней вообще нельзя разговаривать. Это наш самый главный враг.
examples.trans: You mustn't talk to her at all. She is our number-one enemy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'рушить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to destroy, to ruin', paired with 'разрушать'.

examples.text: Ты разрушил мою семью своими фотографиями!
examples.trans: You destroyed my family with your photos!

examples.text: Ты разрушил такой прекрасный и сентиментальный момент!
examples.trans: You ruined such a wonderful and sentimental moment!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'plan' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The mayor came up with a new plan.

examples.text: Но мэр придумал новый план. Сосед мэра теперь пойдёт в мэры.
examples.trans: But the mayor came up with a new plan. The mayor's neighbour will now run for mayor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to seem', paired with 'показаться'.

examples.trans: I think I've seen you somewhere.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучайно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?

examples.text: Здравствуйте! Извините, а вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Hello! Excuse me, are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to find', paired with 'находить'.

examples.text: Ну где я сейчас найду грузчиков?
examples.trans: Well, where am I going to find movers right now?
